title: Task decomposition
task_statement: Split a large task into bounded pieces, merge the results, and check the merged result in code. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Fan-out with a merge step
components.first_principle: Independent pieces run in parallel, and each piece gets a bounded input and a fixed output format. (Inference)

nodes.label: Merge and totals check in code

steps: Divide the source at natural section boundaries.
Send each piece to Claude with its own instructions and a size limit.
Run independent calls in parallel, or send them as a batch when no answer is needed at once.
Collect each piece result in one fixed output format.
Merge the results in code, and check the totals or the citations.
pros: A failed piece can run again alone. (Inference)
Batch processing lowers the token cost for work that can wait.
cons: The merge is one more failure point. (Inference)
Pieces cannot see each other's context unless you pass it. (Inference)
Batch results can take up to 24 hours.
use_when: The pieces are independent, and each piece needs full attention. (Inference)
Each number in the output must cite its source. (Inference)
The work is large and does not need an answer right away.
do_not_use_when: One bounded call with one focus can finish the task. (Inference)
Each step needs the full result of the step before it. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Send the pieces that need no immediate answer through the Message Batches API.
constraints.combination: Keep interactive pieces on the synchronous API. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep each batch under 100,000 requests and 256 MB.
constraints.combination: Split a larger job into several batches.

constraints.choice: Parallelize the pieces when the deadline is short.
constraints.combination: Batch the pieces that can wait up to 24 hours.

constraints.choice: Store the piece ID with each result. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D1.5. Expect a long input with independent sections and a traceability need. The credited answer uses fan-out, limits per piece, and a merge check in code. (Inference)
components.trap: One large call over the whole input. Long inputs weaken focus on the middle parts, and one error fails the whole run. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Split at independent seams, and check the merged result in code.
components.exam_tip: If the stem asks for a check on every number, pick the option with a code check after the merge. (Inference)

components.name: Chain and context control
components.first_principle: Ordered steps pass each output to the next step, so a check between steps keeps an early error out of later steps. (Inference)
steps: Order the steps that depend on the output of an earlier step.
Check each step output in code before the next step starts.
Pass only the fields that the next step needs.
Use compaction when the conversation history nears the context window limit.
Stop the chain at the first failed check, and run that step again alone.
pros: A check between steps localizes an error. (Inference)
Compaction keeps a long task inside the context window without summary code of your own.
Each step gets a small, specific input. (Inference)
cons: Errors compound across steps when no check runs. (Inference)
Latency adds up across sequential steps. (Inference)
Compaction is in beta, and on-demand compaction is the preferred form.
use_when: Step B needs the result of step A.
A long agent task must stay inside the context window.
do_not_use_when: The steps are independent and can run in parallel. (Inference)
One short task fits in one call. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Chain only the steps that need the previous output.
Use on-demand compaction where it is available.
constraints.combination: Use compaction at a token threshold only when on-demand compaction does not fit. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Write each step with one job and a fixed output format. (Inference)
Log each step input and check result. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D1.5. Expect ordered work where an early error would spread. The credited answer chains the steps and checks each output before the next step. (Inference)
components.trap: A chain with no check between steps. The first wrong output becomes the input for every later step. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Chain only the steps that need the previous output, and check each output before the next step.
components.exam_tip: If the stem names an ordered dependency, pick the chain with a check between steps. (Inference)

flowchart TD
  A{Pieces depend on each other?} -->|Yes| B[Chain with check between steps]
  A -->|No| C{Answer needed right away?}

flowchart LR

  S --> P[Parallel pieces]
  S --> C[Ordered chain]
